rationale:
Today's slate is 1 long-form, 3 Shorts and 1 carousel, all inside the GLP-1 focus, across 5 pillars and 4 body areas.

**Long-form choice (Lane A).** This week already has two Lane A long-forms (10-20 and 10-21) and one Lane B (10-22), so one Lane A slot is still open. Two Lane C options were ruled out:
- **CagriSema in women:** the news is more than 48 hours old (announced 10-20), and we ran it as a Short on 10-21, so the 14-day rule blocks a long-form.
- **Retatrutide and kidneys:** the story is under 48 hours old, but it's flagged caution, the primary source isn't confirmed, and it's fast-moving news. That is the profile that keeps failing fact-check.

The CBS retatrutide angle (Lane B) is also blocked, because we covered it in a Short on 10-22. That leaves the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge:
- It's a search question with high buyer intent from older US adults, who bring high ad rates.
- Searches peak through open enrollment (ends Dec 7), and the programme stays relevant until the end of 2027.
- One primary source, Medicare.gov fact sheet 12234, covers it in full.

**Shorts.**
- **13:00 lead (gray-market "what's confirmed?"):** our best repeatable format, with retatrutide named in the title. It uses the NSW Health emergency-department data, which we haven't published yet. The title is deliberately different from 10-22's "Retatrutide Sold Online" so we don't post the same template back to back.
- **08:00 (muscle outcome question):** a single question, not a how-to list. The new fact is the semaglutide handgrip meta-analysis from 19 Oct.
- **20:00 (funnel):** a spin-off of today's long-form, as the planner rules require. It goes out after the long-form is live at 14:00 and names it. It answers a narrower question than the long-form (does the $50 count toward the Part D cap?), which reduces the "same-day Short soaks up demand" risk the playbook warns about.

**Carousel.** Minimum effort, as the playbook asks: it reuses the verified text of the published 10-20 retatrutide type 2 diabetes Short, our best Short so far (223 views), with no new research.

**Topics skipped:**
- The compounded recall: held, because we already ran recall Shorts this week.
- Hair loss: we did a hair-loss long-form on 9-28, inside the 30-day window.
- GLP-1 supplements: we did a supplements carousel on 10-17, also inside the window.
- Halloween: better nearer 28–31 Oct.
- The CagriSema funnel: there's no long-form for it to point to.

pieces.topic: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: $50-a-month GLP-1 medicines for eligible Medicare Part D enrollees (1 Jul 2026 to 31 Dec 2027), explained during open enrollment (Oct 15 to Dec 7, 2026)
pieces.angle:
LANE A (search question); log 'lane: A' in metadata. Series: 'Is a GLP-1 Right for You?'. Build every line from Medicare.gov fact sheet 12234, CMS pages and the official drug labels, each credited and dated with day, month and year. The local TV coverage (WCPO, 22 Oct 2026) may appear only as a one-line hook.

0–15 s: say what viewers will know by the end (who qualifies, which medicines are covered, what you pay, what counts toward the Part D cap, and what to ask your plan). Then give the first concrete answer: the eligibility rule in the fact sheet's own words.

Chapters, named as searched questions:
(1) What is the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?
(2) Who qualifies? Copy the four requirements word for word.
(3) Which medicines are covered? Use the fact sheet's exact product list (the radar says Wegovy injection and tablets, Zepbound KwikPen and Foundayo; confirm each). Generic name first, brand in brackets, and say what each one is FDA-approved for.
(4) How long does it run? 1 Jul 2026 to 31 Dec 2027.
(5) Does the $50 count toward the Part D out-of-pocket cap? Confirm the $2,100 figure and the counting rule from Medicare.gov before using either.
(6) What does open enrollment change for 2027?
(7) What it doesn't cover. Never use compounded, online or no-prescription sources, and say that Medicare and CMS don't call or text asking for card numbers, if a CMS page says so.
(8) Questions to ask your prescriber and your plan.

Re-hook every 45–75 s. One brief line on the common GI side effects (nausea, diarrhoea, constipation). Never give switching advice: 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own.' The subscribe ask comes after the eligibility payoff. End by naming one already-published long-form in the same playlist, then the full prescriber line. US-only label on screen. No dosing. 8–12 min. Publish at 14:00 ET.
pieces.why: Lane A search question with high-ad-rate demand from older US adults that peaks through open enrollment (to Dec 7) and stays relevant until the end of 2027. One official source (Medicare.gov fact sheet 12234) covers it in full, so it can pass fact-check in depth, and we haven't covered it as a Short.

pieces.topic: Unapproved 'retatrutide' peptides and emergency visits: NSW Health data on emergency-department presentations linked to unapproved peptides (July 2025 to September 2026)
pieces.angle: Lead with NSW Health's 19 Oct 2026 release: 1,180 emergency-department presentations linked to unapproved peptide use from 1 July 2025 to 30 September 2026, with monthly presentations rising from 5 to 217. Use the retatrutide share only if the NSW Health epidemiology PDF states it, worded as presentations 'mentioning' retatrutide, and credit it to that document. Drop the 18% admission figure unless the PDF states it. Quote NSW Health's line that these products may contain unknown or harmful substances or the wrong ingredients, and say these are linked presentations, not lab-confirmed contents. Status credited to Lilly with a full date: retatrutide is investigational and not approved anywhere as of Oct 2026, and the real drug exists only in Lilly's trials. Better route: ask a prescriber about approved options or a clinical trial. No sellers or vials, a calm tone, 'Not personal advice' plus the full prescriber line, 170 words or fewer.
pieces.working_title: Retatrutide Peptides and Emergency Visits: What Australia Reported #shorts
pieces.why: Gray-market 'what's confirmed?' Shorts that name retatrutide are our strongest lane (median 103.5 for gray-market Shorts; 120 for retatrutide-named Shorts). The NSW Health data is a new dated fact we haven't published, and the title template differs from 10-22's CBS Short. | fact-check: The primary source exists: NSW Health media release of 19 Oct 2026 (https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/news/Pages/20261019_00.aspx). It confirms 1,180 emergency-department presentations associated with peptide use from 1 July 2025 to 30 September 2026, and monthly presentations rising from 5 in July 2025 to 217 in September 2026. The release names retatrutide only as one of several claimed peptides (BPC-157, GHK-Cu, TB-500, retatrutide, CJC-1295). It doesn't give the 71%, the 833 or the 18% admitted. The 71% appears in press coverage (The Daily Aus, Pharmacy Daily) as visits 'mentioning' or 'naming' retatrutide, and may come from the NSW epidemiology PDF (https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/epidemiology/Publications/unapproved-peptide-use.pdf), which I couldn't extract. The radar's wording 'involving products sold as retatrutide' is stronger than the source: a mention is not confirmed exposure. 18% admitted is unverified, so drop it unless the PDF states it. Use the release's own contents caveat: products 'may contain unknown or harmful substances, be incorrectly labelled or contain different strengths or ingredients than advertised'. The lead format is approved.

pieces.topic: Does semaglutide reduce muscle strength? The Diabetes, Obesity and Metabolism meta-analysis of handgrip strength (19 Oct 2026)
pieces.angle: Title: 'Does Semaglutide Weaken Grip Strength? What Studies Show'. Answer within 10 s: across 10 pooled studies (660 people on semaglutide), average handgrip strength showed no clear change, but the researchers rate the evidence as very low certainty and the studies varied a lot. One line: lean mass (weight) is not the same as strength (function). Separate anchor: in the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy (tirzepatide; adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes; 72 weeks), about a quarter of the weight lost was lean mass. Recommended habits, not proven on the drug: a protein food at each meal unless your clinician has told you to limit protein (for example, kidney disease), and muscle-strengthening activity at least 2 days a week, starting gently. One GI line, 'don't stop or change your medicines on your own', the full prescriber line, and the CTA only if the named long-form is live.
pieces.working_title: Losing Muscle on Semaglutide? What Grip-Strength Studies Show #shorts
pieces.target_keyword: does ozempic make you lose muscle
pieces.why: Muscle outcome questions are proven for us (101 and 131 views). The handgrip-strength result is a fact we haven't published, and the Short funnels to the already-live strength-training long-form. | fact-check: The meta-analysis exists (summarised at https://www.omnicuris.com/medshots/daily_updates/semaglutide-muscle-strength-systematic-review-meta-analysis_20-Oct-26_14-18). 16 reports from 11 unique investigations. 10 studies with 660 semaglutide-treated participants were pooled. Pooled handgrip change −0.16 kgf (95% CI −1.98 to 1.65), not statistically significant. I² was 90.8% with a wide prediction interval, and the authors rate the certainty of the evidence as very low. 'Strength mostly held up' goes further than the paper. Say 'no clear average change, but the evidence is very low certainty and the studies varied a lot'. The change was absolute (kgf). Confirm whether it was also reported relative to body weight, and confirm the journal and online date (the angle says 19 Oct 2026; the summary is dated 20 Oct) on the journal page before scripting. The working title says 'Losing Muscle', but the study measured strength, not muscle mass, so the title has to say strength. SURMOUNT-1 anchor: say 'lean mass', not 'muscle', and label it as a separate tirzepatide trial. Confirm the strength-training long-form is published before naming it in the CTA.

pieces.topic: Tirzepatide (Zepbound) and semaglutide (Wegovy) for $50 a month through the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: does the $50 count toward the Part D out-of-pocket cap?
pieces.angle: Run at 20:00 ET the day after L1 goes live. Title: 'Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: Does the $50 Count Toward Your Cap?' (US). Answer within 10 s, credited to Medicare.gov fact sheet 12234: no, the $50 a month doesn't count toward your Part D deductible or yearly out-of-pocket limit. If you give the cap, say it with its year (2026: $2,100; the 2027 figure as confirmed on Medicare.gov). Covered: Wegovy injection or tablet, Foundayo tablet, and Zepbound KwikPen only (not vials or the single-dose pen). The program runs 1 Jul 2026 to 31 Dec 2027. People with type 2 diabetes, sleep apnea or fatty liver may be covered through their plan instead. Action: during open enrollment (through Dec 7, 2026), ask your plan and prescriber. One GI line, no-switching line, no compounded or online sources, 'Not personal advice' plus the full prescriber line. CTA naming L1's exact published title, with its URL on description line 1 and in the pinned comment.
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide (Zepbound) for $50 on Medicare: What Counts Toward Your Cap? #shorts
pieces.why: Spin-off of L1 and today's funnel Short: it names tirzepatide (median 92 views) and sends Shorts viewers to the high-ad-rate Medicare long-form. | fact-check: The core fact is confirmed in fact sheet 12234: the $50 'doesn't count toward your Medicare drug plan deductible or yearly out-of-pocket limit'. Problems: (1) $2,100 is the 2026 Part D cap. Because this Short frames the question around open enrollment for 2027, the 2027 cap (different; confirm it on Medicare.gov) has to be stated with its year, or leave the dollar figure out. Never present $2,100 as the cap for 2027. (2) Only the Zepbound KwikPen is covered, not the single-dose pen or vials. The working title 'Tirzepatide (Zepbound) for $50' overstates this unless it says KwikPen. (3) The growth playbook says the funnel spin-off runs the DAY AFTER its long-form, not the same day (lesson from 'Tirzepatide Not Working Yet?'). Move it to 20:00 ET on the day after L1, and only once L1 is live, with the exact title L1 actually published under. (4) Mention that people with type 2 diabetes, OSA or fatty liver go through their regular Part D coverage instead.

pieces.topic: Retatrutide in type 2 diabetes: the TRANSCEND-T2D-1 Phase 3 results, reused from the verified 10-20 Short
pieces.angle:
Minimum-effort carousel built only from the verified, published 10-20 S3 script, with no new research. Slides:
(1) The question.
(2) Top-dose weight result vs placebo, with per-arm n, the estimand and 40 weeks, exactly as verified.
(3) The HbA1c line, with its arm and the placebo figure, exactly as verified.
(4) Population: adults whose type 2 diabetes wasn't controlled with diet and exercise alone; placebo-controlled, no tirzepatide arm.
(5) Dated status credited to Lilly: investigational, not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026; a planned filing is not approval.
(6) Common GI side effects; never online products; ask a prescriber about approved options or clinical trials.
(7) Disclaimer, 'don't stop or change your medicines on your own', and the full prescriber line.

No emoji.
